issue.title: Glossary "Proc Shell" still says a proc shell belongs to an agent, but sase-s6 shipped stand-alone xprompt-proc proc shells
issue.description:
The `Proc Shell` glossary definition still says a proc shell belongs to a sase agent.
Epic sase-s6 (`typed_launch_units`, phases sase-s6.5 and sase-s6.7) made that false.

Current definition, in `sase/sase.yml` under `glossary.terms.Proc Shell` (the canonical
source that `sase memory init` renders into `sase/memory/glossary.md`):

> A proc shell is a named supervised proc belonging to a sase agent, with durable
> output and lifecycle state. A family-attached proc shell is a monitor and may carry
> timeout, workspace-claim, and follow-up policy.

What shipped instead: a `%proc` launch unit is stored as lifecycle `proc-shell` with
origin `xprompt-proc` (`src/sase/agent/launch_proc_runtime.py`,
`src/sase/procs/service.py`). It belongs to no agent, is never nested under a family,
allocates no agent runner or agent artifact, and is projected into the Agents tab as its
own row kind counted separately from agents
(`src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_proc_shells.py`; the Agents-tab header renders
`N agents · M procs`).

Verify with:

```bash
sase glossary read "Proc Shell" -r "check whether stand-alone proc shells are covered"
grep -n "belonging to a sase agent" sase/sase.yml
grep -rn "XPROMPT_PROC_ORIGIN" src/sase/procs/ src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_proc_shells.py
```

Proposed change: reword the definition so it covers both an agent-owned proc shell (the
monitor case, which keeps the family-attached sentence) and a stand-alone
`xprompt-proc` proc shell dispatched by a `%proc` launch unit, or split the two into
related terms. Keep `Sase Monitor` accurate as the family-attached specialization.

Closing this requires explicit user permission for the memory edit, then editing
`sase/sase.yml` and running `sase memory init` to regenerate `AGENTS.md`, the provider
instruction shims, and `sase/memory/glossary.md`; `sase memory init --check` must be
clean afterwards.

PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-s6.8 (epic sase-s6). Not edited during the epic because no
explicit user permission for a memory-file edit was given in those conversations.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Reword the "Proc Shell" glossary definition (or split it into related terms) so it covers both agent-owned monitor proc shells and stand-alone xprompt-proc proc shells that belong to no agent, then run sase memory init.
